meta.note: One evolving platform; core tasks fit 20 h/week as planning targets, stretch work costs additional time. Weekly time split is directional: integration counts mainly toward Go/systems. Local GPU feasibility may change the scope of ML exercises. Knowledge checks are recall/demonstration prompts, not additional 20-hour exercises. Senior prompts are optional stretch and do not confer a job title.
meta.costSafety: GCP/Cloud Run/Artifact Registry/Secret Manager and hosted model usage may incur charges; set budgets, check current free-tier terms, and tear down test resources. Do not equate a budget alert with a hard spending cap.

principles: Use this JSON as the source of truth; generated TypeScript must be re-generated, not hand-edited.
Every week has one goal, three focused exercises and an integration deliverable.
Core exercises are required; stretches are optional and outside the 20 h budget.
Record evidence: reproducible tests, benchmarks, failure semantics, version pins and a short ADR.
Defer advanced features until prerequisites are taught; capstone minimums are explicit.
Prefer a single monorepo or closely related services, not 28 isolated demos.
Mark knowledge checklist items only after independently explaining or demonstrating the skill; exercises are tracked separately.
Foundation and intermediate knowledge objectives are the weekly readiness gate; senior architecture questions are optional extensions.

foundation.meaning: Explain core concepts and execute a minimal example independently.
foundation.passRule: Answer the self-check without notes; reproduce a tiny demonstration when applicable.

intermediate.meaning: Implement, debug and test using the weekly coding assignments.
intermediate.passRule: Explain failure cases and demonstrate the relevant behavior in code or benchmarks.

senior.meaning: Evaluate alternatives, design for failure, defend operational tradeoffs and communicate assumptions.
senior.passRule: Write or speak a short design defense supported by measured evidence; optional until core work is complete.

knowledgeChecklistPolicy.sequence: Foundation -> intermediate -> senior stretch -> exercises -> integration evidence.
knowledgeChecklistPolicy.weeklyMasteryRule: A checklist item is complete only if the self-check can be answered independently. Recognition or copying a tutorial does not count.
knowledgeChecklistPolicy.priorityIfBehind: Finish foundations plus intermediate tests and capstone exit criteria before senior stretches; remediate missing baseline items during review time.
knowledgeChecklistPolicy.spacedReview: Revisit weak items after one week and approximately four weeks; use the self-check again without notes.
knowledgeChecklistPolicy.baselinePolicy: Use coreFoundationChecklist as a cumulative gap audit, not as extra mandatory exercises to complete every week.
knowledgeChecklistPolicy.seniorityCaveat: Senior checklist completion demonstrates architectural reasoning, not commercial seniority or production ownership.
